observation_scope: Published mission evidence only; this survey creates no terrain observations, tasks, completed work or execution evidence.
dimension_semantics: All window/context side lengths below are proposed square map-request sizes in metres, not NASA operational requirements, verified footprints or authorised travel distances.

JZ-S01.title: Redox-driven mineral and organic associations in Jezero Crater, Mars
JZ-S01.locator: Abstract; Figure 1 and caption; Figure 2; Outcrop-scale observations
JZ-S01.verified_via: Full primary article text and figure captions opened in browser
JZ-S01.finding: Documents Bright Angel outcrops, several proximity targets, approximate 110 m and 50 m separations, and unresolved biological interpretation.
JZ-S01.limits: Published science context is not a georegistered crop or evidence of life; geographic coordinates were not extracted.

JZ-S02.title: Spatially distributed complex organic matter detected in an ancient river valley in Jezero crater, Mars
JZ-S02.verified_via: Primary paper full text hosted by NIH/PMC
JZ-S02.finding: Raman measurements document robust organic-carbon detections in Bright Angel mudstones; the instrument cannot establish biotic versus abiotic origin.
JZ-S02.limits: Organic material is not confirmed life and is not detectable from the terrain model.

JZ-S03.title: NASA Says Mars Rover Discovered Potential Biosignature Last Year
JZ-S03.locator: Bright Angel/Neretva Vallis context; definition of potential biosignature
JZ-S03.finding: Neretva Vallis is approximately 400 m wide; the Bright Angel finding remains a potential biosignature requiring further investigation.
JZ-S03.limits: The channel-width statement supplies context, not a local route or bounding polygon.

JZ-S04.title: Exploring the Jezero Delta Front: Overview of Results from the Mars 2020 Perseverance Rover's Second Science Campaign
JZ-S04.finding: Maps delta-front targets, stratigraphic sampling and failed abrasions; the floor/delta contact was not clearly exposed at the surface.
JZ-S04.limits: Do not use the malformed traverse-distance number in browser PDF extraction; no exact crop coordinates were derived.

JZ-S05.title: Overview of the Bedrock Geochemistry and Mineralogy Observed by SuperCam During Perseverance's Delta Front Campaign
JZ-S05.finding: Hawksbill Gap and Cape Nukshak are approximately 400 m apart and expose basal delta rocks with varied alteration histories.
JZ-S05.limits: A separation between two localities does not specify their bounding rectangle or a traversable connection.

JZ-S06.title: Comet Geyser: Perseverance's 21st Rock Core
JZ-S06.locator: Bunsen Peak composition and origin discussion; final travel paragraph
JZ-S06.finding: Bunsen Peak's sampled rock contains carbonate and silica; its origin remained under investigation, with difficult block-and-sand terrain discussed farther along the journey.
JZ-S06.limits: Do not label the whole Margin Unit as a confirmed ancient shoreline or infer material strength from the DEM.

JZ-S07.title: NASA's Perseverance Mars Rover to Take Bite Out of Krokodillen
JZ-S07.locator: Opening paragraphs describing location, boundary and plateau area
JZ-S07.verified_via: Official NASA article; publication date independently verified by root agent
JZ-S07.finding: Krokodillen is an approximately 30 ha rocky plateau west and south of Witch Hazel Hill, near the rim/plains geological boundary.
JZ-S07.limits: Area alone gives neither polygon shape nor a safe access corridor.

JZ-S08.title: Clay Minerals From Mars' Most Ancient Past?
JZ-S08.locator: Krokodillen, Strong Island and Laknes discussion; final paragraph
JZ-S08.finding: SuperCam detected clay signatures in Krokodillen bedrock; their spatial variability motivated further contextual exploration.
JZ-S08.limits: No uniform mineral distribution or exact target coordinates are supplied by this survey.

JZ-S09.title: NASA's Perseverance Mars Rover Studies Trove of Rocks on Crater Rim
JZ-S09.finding: Describes diverse crater-rim rocks, a roughly 135 m-high slope and approximately 110 m and 160 m separations between investigations.
JZ-S09.limits: Distances are contextual, not exact route lengths or proof that all targets fit a selected window.

JZ-S10.title: Stratigraphy Preserved on the Jezero Crater Rim Reveals Repeated Impacts on Early Mars
JZ-S10.verified_via: Primary JGR Planets article full text
JZ-S10.finding: Studies a roughly 75 m-thick Broom Point succession, deformation and evidence interpreted as repeated ancient impacts.
JZ-S10.limits: Stratigraphic thickness is not horizontal crop size, operational climb distance or terrain safety.

candidates.name: Bright Angel - Beaver Falls, Neretva Vallis
candidates.region: Western Jezero inlet channel, northern Bright Angel outcrops
candidates.science_question: How do mudstone facies, contacts and alteration vary over a short documented corridor?
observed_basis: Published rover investigations document several targets in the Beaver Falls workspace, including Cheyava Falls, Apollo Temple and Steamboat Mountain.
The Nature Figure 1 caption places Beaver Falls about 110 m upslope of Walhalla Glades and Grapevine Canyon about 50 m downslope of that workspace.
Published Raman and mineralogical studies establish scientifically interesting organic-bearing mudstones, without confirming biological origin.
Neretva Vallis is reported as approximately 400 m wide.
proposed_secondary_opportunities: Inspect contrasting textures and fracture or vein exposures encountered within the selected public corridor, if independently visible in the declared inputs.
Compare an accessible adjacent lithology before considering optional sampling; do not count the already-published target names as new software discoveries.
Use local reconnaissance to test whether the selected contact or workspace can be approached and returned from within unchanged reserves.
limitations: No exact 128 m crop is verified; a workspace is different from the full channel and both margins.
A 20 m DEM cannot reveal submetre nodules, organic material or mineral chemistry.
No route, soil mechanics, instrument capability or consumable feasibility has been demonstrated for this proposed crop.

candidates.name: Hawksbill Gap - Hogwallow Flats - Skinner and Wildcat Ridge
candidates.science_question: Can a local section preserve meaningful changes in sedimentary facies and alteration while offering alternative inspection targets?
observed_basis: Published campaign maps and sample records document stratigraphic investigations and multiple real sampling targets.
The campaign also documents failed abrasions associated with target fracturing or subsidence, providing real examples of scientific interest without assured sample suitability.
proposed_secondary_opportunities: Compare changes in layering, visible grain or clast character and fracture exposures along a selected accessible outcrop section.
Evaluate an alternative nearby inspection target when the primary surface is unsuitable for contact work, using explicit public evidence rather than DEM-derived material strength.
limitations: Do not claim that all named targets fit one proposed square or can be visited within one resource allocation.
Potential preservation of biosignatures is not confirmed life or an automatic detection of organic matter.
No rock strength, friction or sample suitability is inferred from elevation.

candidates.name: Cape Nukshak - Enchanted Lake - Cannery Passage
candidates.region: Basal western Jezero delta and adjacent crater floor
candidates.science_question: What can exposed basal layers establish about the delta/floor relationship when the contact is partly obscured?
observed_basis: Published mission observations identify Enchanted Lake as low delta sedimentary exposures near Cape Nukshak.
The floor/delta contact was not clearly resolved at the surface because of cover and erosion; radar informed its interpretation.
Hawksbill Gap and Cape Nukshak are reported as approximately 400 m apart.
proposed_secondary_opportunities: Inspect separate exposed layers or edges of cover along a selected corridor without inventing a visible contact where it is hidden.
Use the contrast between observable outcrop and obscured context as an explicit incomplete-evidence case.
limitations: A 128 m square cannot span two localities 400 m apart.
No radar capability or subsurface observation is added to the simulated agents.
An inferred subsurface relationship does not establish a directly observable surface boundary.

candidates.name: Margin Unit - Bunsen Peak
candidates.science_question: How does an accessible carbonate/silica-bearing workspace relate to the surrounding unit and its alteration history?
observed_basis: Published Comet Geyser sample investigations identify carbonate and silica at Bunsen Peak.
The cited mission update explicitly keeps the rock's origin under investigation.
proposed_secondary_opportunities: Compare exposed surfaces, adjacent textures and fracture or vein features where visible in declared public imagery.
Choose an optional comparison target only after compatible inspection and return-resource checks; no mineral classification is generated from the DEM.
limitations: The whole Margin Unit is not assumed to be a confirmed ancient shoreline or uniform carbonate exposure.
Origin and alteration hypotheses are not resolved by this literature survey.
A local workspace and its operational route remain to be independently selected and validated.

candidates.name: Krokodillen - Laknes and Strong Island context
candidates.region: Outer western Jezero crater rim, downslope west and south of Witch Hazel Hill
candidates.science_question: How do clay-bearing exposures and other materials vary across the rim/plains boundary?
observed_basis: NASA describes an approximately 30 ha rocky plateau near an important rim/plains geological boundary.
Published SuperCam observations at Krokodillen identify clay signatures with spatial variability and contextual follow-up around abrasion workspaces.
proposed_secondary_opportunities: Compare accessible exposures with differing published or newly evidenced spectral/texture character rather than assuming uniform clay distribution.
Investigate an additional local contact or surface only when it is visible and does not compromise primary work and return.
limitations: A 128 m square covers only 1.6384 ha; the reported 30 ha plateau has an unverified irregular footprint.
A 512 m square has 26.2144 ha area and is not demonstrated to cover the plateau; 1 km is a proposed context request, not a travel requirement.
No complete mineral distribution or exact Strong Island/Laknes coordinates are supplied.

candidates.name: Witch Hazel Hill - Broom Point and Tablelands context
candidates.science_question: Can diverse ancient rocks, deformation and impact-related stratigraphy be investigated without exceeding access and return constraints?
observed_basis: Published rover investigations describe diverse rocks on a roughly 135 m-high slope, with nearby investigations separated by about 110 m and 160 m.
A 2026 primary study examines an approximately 75 m-thick Broom Point succession and interprets evidence for repeated ancient impacts.
Published sample context identifies Tablelands as a serpentinite target; this is archival mission evidence, not a model-derived detection.
proposed_secondary_opportunities: Compare accessible stratigraphic or textural contrasts from a selected low-relief workspace, if public data justify access.
Use a scientifically attractive but resource-infeasible target as an explicit rejection case rather than relaxing reserves to obtain acceptance.
limitations: The reported 75 m is stratigraphic thickness, not a horizontal crop side or safe climb distance.
The full 135 m relief is not assumed to be traversed by any proposed local mission.
Scientific diversity does not establish human or rover access, material strength, feasible service or return within current budgets.
Candidate names are published mission-locality names; they are not operational task identifiers or claims of new discoveries.
Exact geographic crop bounds, base locations, cell centres, current-dataset coverage and executable routes remain unverified.
This catalog neither changes approved scenario values nor imports a science layer, observation, planner or evaluator dataset.
Public HiRISE asset availability does not authorise reusing data reserved for the evaluator as a planning prior.
No coefficients, physical tolerances, scientific profiles or operational budgets are approved by this survey.
